topic.title: Sparse Signal Recovery and Dictionary Identifiability
topic.area: Sparsity, Low-Rank Models, and Dimensionality Reduction
topic.overview: Sparse recovery reconstructs signals from limited measurements by assuming that only a small number of components are active. This cluster includes compressed sensing, mixtures of sparse regressions, dictionary learning, and sparse autoencoders. The common question is when the observations determine a useful sparse representation and whether an algorithm can recover it reliably.
topic.whyItMatters: Good reconstruction does not automatically make a representation unique or interpretable. Recovery guarantees, robustness to imperfect sparsity, and stability across training runs help distinguish meaningful structure from arbitrary choices made by the learning procedure.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives concern independent components, denoising, and sparse coding. Later work extends recovery to one-bit observations and unknown mixtures. Recent sparse-autoencoder research reconnects neural concept dictionaries to classical identifiability conditions, modifying architectures and training to reduce instability while improving reconstruction.
openQuestions: Which identifiability conditions can be checked on learned dictionaries rather than merely assumed?
How robust are recovered concepts when the underlying representation is only approximately sparse?

papers.title: Distributed Machine Learning with Sparse Heterogeneous Data
papers.tldr: Coupling sparse local models through sparse graph differences can reduce sample requirements under the paper's stated recovery conditions.

papers.title: Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares for Basis Pursuit with Global Linear Convergence Rate
papers.tldr: An IRLS variant has global linear convergence from any initialization when measurements satisfy the null space property.

papers.title: On learning sparse vectors from mixture of responses
papers.tldr: The paper establishes algorithms for sparse-vector support recovery from noisy mixed sign responses and conditional approximate recovery from noiseless responses.

papers.title: Support Recovery of Sparse Signals from a Mixture of Linear Measurements
papers.tldr: Algorithms recover every sparse component’s support from mixed linear or one-bit measurements with high-probability measurement guarantees.

papers.title: Towards Sample-Optimal Compressive Phase Retrieval with Sparse and Generative Priors
papers.tldr: Near-optimal measurement guarantees for phase retrieval motivate a practical initializer, while computing the globally optimal solutions covered by the theory remains challenging.

papers.title: Equivariant Priors for compressed sensing with unknown orientation
papers.tldr: Equivariant generative priors enable latent-space reconstruction of compressed signals with unknown orientation, supported by theoretical recovery guarantees.

papers.title: Provable Domain Generalization via Invariant-Feature Subspace Recovery
papers.tldr: Invariant-feature Subspace Recovery uses distribution moments to obtain domain-generalization guarantees and improve reported worst-case accuracy under spurious correlations.

papers.title: Uncertainty Modeling in Generative Compressed Sensing
papers.tldr: CS-BGM models uncertainty in latent variables and generator parameters to expand reconstruction possibilities in generative compressed sensing.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on Randomly Preconditioned Lasso via Robust Sparse Designs
papers.tldr: Randomized invertible preconditioning cannot remove certain sample barriers for Lasso.

papers.title: Signal Recovery with Non-Expansive Generative Network Priors
papers.tldr: A weaker matrix condition extends generative-prior signal recovery guarantees to Gaussian networks that can include contractive layers.

papers.title: Hiding Data Helps: On the Benefits of Masking for Sparse Coding
papers.tldr: A masking objective can favor true dictionary recovery where standard noisy, over-realized sparse coding objectives can fail.

papers.title: One-Step Estimator for Permuted Sparse Recovery
papers.tldr: The paper gives recovery lower bounds and a simple estimator for identifying missing measurement correspondences in undersampled sparse recovery.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Uniform Signal Recovery in Nonlinear Generative Compressed Sensing
papers.tldr: A unified framework gives nearly the same measurement requirements for recovering an entire generative signal family as for recovering a single fixed signal.

papers.title: Global Identifiability of $\ell_1$-based Dictionary Learning via Matrix Volume Optimization
papers.tldr: A volume-minimizing dictionary learning formulation guarantees global recovery under stated coefficient conditions and only nonsingularity of the dictionary.

papers.title: Information Maximization Perspective of Orthogonal Matching Pursuit with Applications to Explainable AI
papers.tldr: The paper connects information-based query selection to sparse coding and uses that connection for efficient, concept-based image explanations.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Learning with Nonlinear Model Classes from Arbitrary Linear Samples
papers.tldr: A unified theory connects linear measurement schemes and nonlinear model classes to data requirements for near-best generalization.

papers.title: Exponential Spectral Pursuit: An Effective Initialization Method for Sparse Phase Retrieval
papers.tldr: ESP improves sparse phase-retrieval initialization through a tighter sampling-complexity bound and stronger empirical performance.

papers.title: Straight-Through Meets Sparse Recovery: the Support Exploration Algorithm
papers.tldr: SEA applies the straight-through estimator to sparse recovery, improving experimental support selection while providing guarantees under comparatively stricter sufficient conditions.

papers.title: Sparse Bayesian Generative Modeling for Compressive Sensing
papers.tldr: A sparse Bayesian generative prior learns from limited noisy compressed data and supports reconstruction with uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: The Iterative Optimal Brain Surgeon: Faster Sparse Recovery by Leveraging Second-Order Information
papers.tldr: Using loss curvature in sparse-recovery projection steps improves convergence guarantees under suitable assumptions and strengthens practical sparse-model training.

papers.title: Exact Recovery of Sparse Binary Vectors from Generalized Linear Measurements
papers.tldr: Linear estimation achieves optimal sample complexity for exact sparse binary recovery from noisy one-bit measurements, with tight results also obtained for logistic regression.

papers.title: Efficient $k$-Sparse Band–Limited Interpolation with Improved Approximation Ratio
papers.tldr: A hierarchical noise-cancellation framework sharply improves provable approximation factors for efficient sparse band-limited signal interpolation.

papers.title: Sparse Polyak: an adaptive step size rule for high-dimensional M-estimation
papers.tldr: Sparse Polyak adapts optimization step sizes using restricted smoothness to improve high-dimensional statistical estimation.

papers.title: The Price of Sparsity: Sufficient Conditions for Sparse Recovery using Sparse and Sparsified Measurements
papers.tldr: The paper quantifies sparse-measurement sample complexity and gives a separate, conjecture-dependent sufficient bound for sparsifying dense measurements.

papers.title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: Small architectural and training changes make sparse autoencoders more stable, with lower reconstruction error and near-identifiable sparse codes.
